image_description: A close-up, high-resolution photograph of a grey whale's head and upper body surfacing in green ocean water. The image prominently features the whale's small eye, mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches (callosities), and the arched rostrum. Water splashes around the lower portion of the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight close-up of the side of the head/eye region. The top of the rostrum and blowholes are outside the frame or obscured by the angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white callosities/barnacle clusters surrounding the eye and on the rostrum.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal area/posterior back is not visible in this close-up shot of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only a fragment of the body is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified from this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head checkpoint; the visible skin exhibits the correct mottling and barnacle distribution.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and underwater/not visible; baleen plates cannot be seen.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located ventrally and posterior to the head; they are not visible in this frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high resolution allows verification of the rough, bumpy texture associated with cyamid infestations and barnacles.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification based on the unique skin mottling and head shape, distinguishing it from other cetaceans.
To analyze the realism of the water splashes, refraction, and skin wetness, ensuring no AI-generated 'smearing' or texture inconsistencies.
To verify the structural integrity of the eye and the sharpness of the boundary between the whale and the water, checking for melting artifacts.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Focus heavily on the micro-texture of the skin. AI generators often struggle with the specific chaotic distribution of barnacles vs. natural skin pigmentation. Verify if the 'white patches' look like attached organisms (3D depth) or just painted-on noise. Check the eye for realistic corneal reflection and moisture.
